Post site contact mobile number and site manager name at main occupant entrance and common areas — update weekly.

Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts

tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from scaffold — erection incomplete or not yet load-tested
controls: Obtain and review scaffold design certificate from licenced engineer before any component is delivered to site.
Barricade scaffold erection zone to exclude occupants and non-essential personnel during assembly — minimum 2m exclusion radius at ground level.
Install edge protection (guardrails 1.0–1.15 m high, toe boards 150 mm) before any worker accesses the working platform.
Conduct pre-use check of all scaffold components (tubes, fittings, couplers, base plates) for deformation, cracks, corrosion — record on site checklist.
Load-test completed scaffold to 1.5 × working load using certified calibrated weights before handover certificate is issued.
Obtain handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder confirming design, load test, and edge protection complete before first worker accesses platform.
Brief all workers on scaffold design limits, load capacity, and no-entry zones before work commences.
Verify wind speed <40 km/h before erection commences — stop work if wind exceeds limit.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start load testing until: all edge protection, guardrails, and platform boards are fully installed and secured.

🛑 STOP WORK if: load test fails or load-bearing capacity cannot be confirmed — do not allow worker access until re-tested and signed off.

tasks.task: Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed, and tile bed
tasks.scope: Strip membrane, screed, and tile to expose slab. Dust control and wet suppression. Hazardous material screening (asbestos, ACM) before removal. Debris collection and management.
hazards: Inhalation of dust and particles — membrane, screed, and tile debris
Asbestos exposure — ACM in screed, adhesive, or membrane (if pre-1990s product)
Struck by falling debris — inadequate containment or edge control during stripping
Skin and eye irritation — cement dust and wet suppression mist
Slip on wet surface — water suppression creating slippery working platform
tasks.dominant_hazard: Asbestos exposure — ACM in screed, adhesive, or membrane (if pre-1990s product)
controls: Before stripping commences, obtain material sample from membrane, screed, and adhesive bed. Send to NATA-registered laboratory for asbestos identification. Do not proceed until results received and interpreted.

If asbestos confirmed in membrane, screed, or adhesive: stop work. tell site supervisor and project manager. Engage licensed asbestos removal contractor to plan and execute removal under controlled conditions per Work Health and Safety Regulation 2017 Schedule 3 cl.6.
If asbestos results negative: establish wet suppression system. Wet down all surfaces before mechanical breakout. Maintain continuous mist spray during stripping to suppress dust generation.

Install dust extraction unit with HEPA filter attached to mechanical tools (grinder, breaker). Position extraction nozzle within 150 mm of cutting or grinding point. Run extraction continuously during tool use.

Establish exclusion zone. Barricade perimeter with site mesh or dust barrier to prevent debris escape and falling material. Position catch net or containment frame below stripping zone to contain falling tiles and screed pieces.
Wear half-mask respirator P2 (or equivalent) during dry stripping or if dust escapes suppression system. Fit test required before first use. Replace filter when resistance increases.
Wear eye protection
Monitor water levels on slab surface. Stop work if water pooling creates slip hazard. Direct water to nominated drainage point. Dry walkways with towel or squeegee before each break.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start mechanical stripping until: asbestos laboratory results received, interpreted, and clearance confirmed by supervisor or project manager
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not use mechanical breaker or grinder until: dust extraction system tested and operating at full capacity; exclusion zone and catch net installed and confirmed secure
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos test result is positive — engage licensed contractor and do not disturb material further
🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression system fails or dust escapes exclusion zone during breakout — restart suppression and confirm extraction before resuming
🛑 STOP WORK if: water pooling on slab creates slip hazard or worker slips — dry surface and review water management before work continues
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

eye protection

monitoring.frequency: Before each use; continuous during tool operation; 30-minute checks if suppression is manual
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of mist spray over work area; absence of visible dust cloud at exclusion zone boundary; HEPA filter resistance reading below maximum on extraction unit gauge

tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — working at balcony level without guardrail protection during investigation

Establish exclusion zone below balcony edge — minimum 2 m wide, barricaded and signed. No access for occupants during work.
Wear fall arrest harness with lanyard secured to fixed anchor point before approaching slab edge. Anchor must be verified by supervisor.

Isolate the work area with temporary screening or polythene barriers to prevent contact between workers and crack sealant or primer.
Confirm ground conditions and edge protection system before starting work at slab edge or elevated platform.

tasks.dominant_hazard: Chemical exposure — liquid membrane volatiles or sheet membrane adhesive fume in occupied space
controls: Obtain and display SDS for membrane product on point of use before application starts.
Confirm substrate is clean, dry, and temperature within manufacturer's minimum before membrane application.
Ventilate space continuously during and 4 hours after application — open windows and install temporary extraction fan to occupied areas.
Apply membrane in 2m² maximum sections to control volatile release and allow real-time ventilation monitoring.
Barricade wet membrane surface with tape and signage — prohibit pedestrian crossing until cured per product data sheet.
Isolate occupied spaces downwind of application area — close internal doors and use temporary plastic sheeting to seal vents.
Check all penetration seals and upturns are complete before membrane has set — do not allow partial cure.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves, respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum for liquid; full-face P3 for sheet adhesive), and hi-viz shirt or vest

tasks.scope: Pour and finish levelling screed, tile bed adhesive and grout, waterproofing continuity at edges and penetrations.

Back or muscle strain — manual tile bed adhesive application or grout mixing
Slip on wet screed or adhesive — surface not yet cured
Fall from height — working at slab perimeter during edge finishing or upturns
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — working at slab perimeter during edge finishing or upturns
controls: Install perimeter edge protection (guardrail or fall-arrest anchor) before any worker approaches slab edge. Anchor point must be rated for suspended load and certified before use.
Wet-finish all screed surfaces immediately after pouring to suppress dust. Do not dry-finish or allow dust to drift into occupied spaces below.
Apply tile bed adhesive only after screed has fully cured and passed hardness check. Do not walk on or work from wet screed.
Barricade wet screed perimeter with hazard tape and signage. Restrict access to authorised personnel only until surface is trafficable.
Use premixed tile bed adhesive or cement-based adhesive from sealed containers with product SDS on site. Do not hand-mix adhesive in open air.
Provide mechanical mixing and pump application for adhesive where possible. If hand-mixing required, use powered paddle mixer — no hand-stirring of dry powder.
Wear dust mask (P2) during screed finishing. Remove and store mask in clean bag when wet work starts.
Wear non-slip footwear always on wet or cured screed surfaces.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not pour screed until: edge protection (guardrail or certified anchor) is installed, inspected, and signed off by site supervisor or scaffold licenced worker.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply tile bed adhesive until: screed surface is fully cured (minimum 7 days), hardness checked, and surface is clean and dry.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker approaches slab edge without harness attached to certified anchor, or edge protection is removed or damaged.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wet screed or uncured adhesive is occupied by personnel below the slab without exclusion zone in place.
🛑 STOP WORK if: screed dust is observed drifting into occupied spaces, or dust control (wet finishing) is not maintained.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

hazards: Fall from height — removal and reinstatement of balustrade bolts exposes unprotected edge
Struck by hand tool — bolt tightening or tile cutting with angle grinder
Repetitive strain — tile laying and grouting over extended period

tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — removal and reinstatement of balustrade bolts exposes unprotected edge
controls: Erect perimeter edge protection (guardrail minimum 1.1 m high) along balcony perimeter before any worker enters work area.
Install catch platform or debris net below balcony during tile cutting and bolt reinstatement to contain falling tools or debris.
Wear harness and lanyard attached to secure anchor point when removing or reinstating balustrade bolts near unprotected edges.
Cut tiles using wet saw or wet grinder with water suppression — no dry cutting on balcony.
Apply tile grout only during weather window: ambient temperature 5–30°C, no rain forecast within 24 hours, relative humidity <80%.
Seal membrane penetrations around balustrade bolt holes using compatible waterproofing sealant before reinstating bolts.
Use power tool (not manual) to tighten balustrade bolts to engineer-specified torque — record in site logbook.
Rotate workers between tile laying and grouting tasks to reduce repetitive strain — no worker to perform same task >4 consecutive hours.

Barricade wet screed perimeter with hazard tape and signage. Restrict access to authorised personnel only until surface is trafficable.
Use premixed tile bed adhesive or cement-based adhesive from sealed containers with product SDS on site. Do not hand-mix adhesive in open air.

Wear non-slip footwear always on wet or cured screed surfaces.

Establish exclusion zone 4 m radius around scaffold footprint. Barricade and delineate. No occupant or vehicle access during dismantling.
Brief all occupants in writing 48 hours before dismantling. Confirm alternative access route is clear and safe.
Remove all loads, ties, and suspended items from scaffold. check all connection points and ledger bolts for tightness before start.
Dismantle top-down only. Remove one bay or level at a time. Support remaining structure after each component removal — do not leave hanging or loose sections.
Catch or lower all components to ground using rope and control method — no drop, throw, or free-fall of any component from height.
Assign dedicated spotter at ground level. Spotter confirms ground clear before each component descent. Brief communication protocol to dismantler.
Place all scaffold components in designated storage area. Stack feet, plates, and loose items on flat ground. Do not leave feet or bases across site walkways.
